svg.title: Four elections that people confuse: IGMP querier, PIM DR, assert winner and bidirectional DF
svg.desc: A two by two grid. Querier: Layer 2 election, lowest IP address in the subnet wins, decides whether the snooping table is refreshed; wrong querier means the table ages out. PIM DR: Layer 3 election on a multi-access LAN, highest priority then highest IP wins, decides who sends joins and registers for the whole segment; two DRs or a wrong DR means duplicate or missing registers. Assert winner: per (S,G), compared on metric and then administrative distance, decides which of two parallel paths forwards onto the shared LAN, and the loser prunes. Bidirectional DF: per group, elected toward the RP, one DF per RP per LAN, decides who forwards downstream and who sends the join upstream. No election ever involves all four at once, which is why the wrong one gets blamed.
svg.text: Four elections, four different questions
"Who is the DR" and "who is the querier" are not the same question, and neither of them is the assert winner.
1. IGMP QUERIER
Layer 2, per subnet
Elected by: lowest IP address on the segment.
Decides: who sends the periodic general query
that refreshes the snooping table.
ip igmp snooping querier <SVI address>
Wrong or missing: the table ages out at 260 s,
video freezes periodically. No PIM involved.
Note: this is not a PIM election. It exists even
in a VLAN with no router at all.
2. PIM DR
Layer 3, per multi-access LAN
Elected by: highest priority, then highest IP.
Decides: who sends joins, prunes and registers
on behalf of the whole segment.
ip pim dr-priority 100
Wrong DR: a suboptimal first hop, or a register
that never happens because the DR is not the
RPF neighbour of the source.
On point-to-point links there is no election: the
only neighbour is the DR.
3. ASSERT WINNER
Per (S,G) or per (*,G), on one LAN
Elected by: lowest metric to the source, then
lowest administrative distance.
Decides: which of two routers forwards the
stream onto the shared segment. The loser
prunes its own OIL for that (S,G).
Purpose: prevents duplicate packets on a LAN
when both routers have the stream.
Symptom of a stuck assert: duplicated packets
on a shared segment, invisible at Layer 3.
4. BIDIRECTIONAL DF
Per group, per RP, on one LAN
Elected by: lowest metric toward the RP, then
highest IP as tie-break.
Decides: who forwards downstream traffic and
who sends the (*,G) join toward the RP.
One DF per RP per LAN, so a segment can have
several DFs for several RPs.
Symptom of two DFs: duplicated downstream
traffic and multicast storms on the segment.
Ask which election before you ask which router: querier is Layer 2, DR is Layer 3, assert is per (S,G), DF is bidirectional-only. The commands that show them are also different.
